κλη θῶμεν ἐπὶ δίαιταν ἀδελφῶν, ὥστε διαιτῆσαι τὰ κατ' αὐτούς. ΚΕΦ. ΛΒʹ. Στίχ. αʹ.
Καὶ ἐπαύσατο Ἰὼβ ῥήμασιν. Ἡσύχασαν δὲ καὶ οἱ τρεῖς φίλοι αὐτοῦ ἔτι ἀντειπεῖν Ἰώβ.
Ἦν γὰρ Ἰὼβ δίκαιος ἐναντίον αὐτῶν. Οὐχ ἁπλῶς ἐπαύσατο. Καρδία δὲ ἦν αὐτοῦ
νοοῦσα τὰ θεῖα, οὐκ ἐπαύσατο. Ἤδη γὰρ καιρὸς τῷ παντὶ πράγματι ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανὸν,
καιρὸς τοῦ σιγᾷν καὶ καιρὸς τοῦ λαλεῖν. Ὅτε οὖν καιρὸς τοῦ ἀποκρίνασθαι πρὸς τοὺς
τρεῖς, ἔλεγεν· ὅτε ἦν καιρὸς, μετὰ τὸ ἐπι στομίσαι αὐτοὺς, ἐσίγησε. Καὶ οἶμαι ἐν
ἐπαίνῳ λέ γεσθαι τὸ, Ἐπαύσατο ὁ Ἰώβ. Στίχ. ζʹ. ∆ιὸ ἡσύχασα, φοβηθεὶς τοῦ ὑμῖν ἀναγ
γεῖλαι τὴν ἐμαυτοῦ ἐπιστήμην. Ἐπιστήμην ἔχει, πῶς ἄνθρωποι πάσχουσι· διὰ τί
ἄνθρωποι ἐν περιστάσεσί τισιν ἐν τῷ βίῳ τούτῳ μόνῳ γίνονται· ὅσοι ἄδικοι ὄντες

ἐσαλεύθησαν οἱ πόδες. Ἐὰν ἐν τῷ βίῳ τούτῳ μόνον ἐνίδω, παρ' ὀλίγον ἐξεχύθη τὰ
διαβήματά μου. Στίχ. ιʹ. Οὐχ οἱ πολυχρόνιοί εἰσι σοφοί. Οὐ γὰρ ἀνάγκη, φησὶ, τοὺς
πρεσβύτας μόνους εἶναι σοφούς· ἀλλ' ἔστι καὶ ἀπὸ νεότητος ἀκοῦσαί τι γενναῖον. Εἰ
γὰρ χρόνος ποιεῖ σοφοὺς, πολλῷ μᾶλλον Θεός. Στίχ. ιηʹ. Ὠλέκει γάρ με τὸ πνεῦμα
τῆς γαστρός. Ὥσπερ τις ἔγκυος γίνεται, καὶ μορφωθέντος τοῦ γεννωμένου ἐν αὐτῷ,
ἐπὶ ὠδῖνας ἔρχεται, μέχρις οὗ ἀπογεννήσῃ τοῦτο ὃ πρότερον συνείληφε· τοιοῦ τόν τί
μοι νόει γενέσθαι καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς τοῦ φιλομα θοῦς ψυχῆς. Συλλαμβάνει γὰρ τὸν λόγον
ὃν ἀπαγγελ λόμενον μορφοῖ καὶ τυποῖ αὐτὸν τῇ τάξει. Ὅτ' ἂν δὲ μετὰ τὸ τυπῶσαι
καὶ μορφῶσαι αὐτὸν ἕτοιμον γενόμε νον, μὴ ὡς ἔκτρωμα ἀνέτοιμον καὶ ἀτελὲς
παραδιδῷ, ἀλλ' ὡς τελεσφορηθὲν καὶ τετελειωμένον εἴποιμι ἄν. Στίχ. ιθʹ. Ἡ δὲ
γαστήρ μου ὥσπερ ἀσκὸς γλεύκους ζέων δεδεμένος. ∆οκεῖ μοι ἐντεῦθεν εἰρῆσθαι τὸ
ἐν τῷ Εὐαγγελίῳ. 17.96 Οὐδεὶς οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιοὺς βάλλει Στίχ. κʹ.

Οὐκ ἔχω ταύτην τὴν ἐπιστήμην, ἵνα θαυμάσω πρόσωπον· ἀλλὰ καταφρονῶ
ἀνθρώπων, καὶ τῆς παρ' αὐτοῖς αἰ σχύνης βροτῶν, καὶ τῆς παρ' αὐτοῖς ἐντροπῆς.
Στίχ. κβʹ. Εἰ δὲ μὴ, καὶ ἐμὲ σῆτες ἔδονται. Ὡς τῶν σητῶν διεσθιόντων τοὺς
λαμβάνοντας πρόσ ωπα ἀνθρώπων. ΚΕΦ. ΛΕʹ. Στίχ. ʹ. Εἰ ἥμαρτες, τί πράξεις; Ἐὰν
ἀναβλέψῃς εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν, καὶ κατανοήσῃς τὰ νέφη, νοήσεις τί ἥμαρτες. Τί σε
πρᾶξαι δεῖ; Προσέρχεσθαι τῷ ἀρχιερεῖ, καὶ παρακαλεῖν, ἵνα ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς προσαγάγῃ
θυσίαν περὶ σοῦ. Ἐὰν γάρ τις ἁμάρτῃ, παράκλητον ἔχομεν πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα Ἰησοῦν
Χριστὸν δίκαιον, καὶ αὐτὸς ἱλασμός ἐστι περὶ τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων ἡμῶν. Στίχ. ʹ. Εἰ δὲ
καὶ πολλὰ ἠνόμησας, τί δύνασαι ποιῆσαι; Τὸ τηλικοῦτον ποιήσεις· ἀναλύσεις σου τὰς
πολλὰς ἀνομίας. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀνιάτοις, οἷς ἑαυ τοὺς ἰάσασθαι οὐ δυνάμεθα,
ἦλθεν Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἐξ οὐρανῶν, ἵνα τὰ ἀνίατα ἰάσηται, καὶ γίνηται τό· Μακάριοι,
ὧν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἀνομίαι, καὶ ὧν ἀπε καλύφθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι. Στίχ. ζʹ. Ἐπειδὴ οὖν
δίκαιος εἶ, τί δώσεις αὐτῷ; Ἀλλ' εἰ δίκαιος εἶ ὡς πρὸς Θεὸν, τί ἔχεις δοῦναι κατὰ τὴν
σὴν δικαιοσύνην; Εἰ δὲ καὶ ὡς λέγεις δίκαιος εἶ, τί προσθήσεις αὐτῷ; Στίχ. ιʹ. Ὁ
κατατάσσων φυλακὰς νυκτερινάς. Ἐγκώμια τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ αἴνους καὶ ὕμνους αὐτοῦ
διεξέρχεται. Ὁ κατατάσσων φυλακὰς νυκτε ρινὰς, αὐτὸς ὁ Θεός ἐστι. Θέλω ἰδεῖν,
πῶς κατατάσσων ἐστὶν ὁ Θεὸς φυ λακὰς νυκτερινάς. Ὅλως ὁ αἰὼν οὗτος νύξ ἐστι,
σκό τος ἐστί. Τὸ φῶς τηρεῖταί σοι. Ὃ βλέπεις νῦν φῶς, δι' ἐσόπτρου βλέπεις· Καὶ ἐν
τῷ φωτί σου ὀψόμεθα φῶς. Μέλλομέν ποτε βλέπειν αὐτό. Οὐκοῦν νύξ ἐστι πᾶς ὁ
αἰών· ἐπεὶ νύξ ἐστι, πόλεμοι πολλοὶ, πολ λὰ θηρία περιέρχεται. Στίχ. ιαʹ. Ὁ διορίζων
με ἀπὸ τετραπόδων γῆς. Ἐὰν ᾖς ἁμαρτωλὸς, οὐ διωρίσθης ἀπὸ τῶν τετραπόδων γῆς.
Ἄνθρωπος γὰρ ἐν τιμῇ ὢν, οὐ συνῆκε. Παρασυνεβλήθη τοῖς κτήνεσι τοῖς ἀνοή τοις,
καὶ ὡμοιώθη αὐτοῖς. Ἐὰν ᾖς ἁμαρτωλὸς, οὐ διωρίσθης ἀπὸ τῶν τετραπόδων τῆς γῆς·
ἀλλὰ λέγε ταί σοι· Μὴ γίνεσθε ὡς ἵππος καὶ ἡμίονος, οἷς οὐκ 17.97 ἔστι σύνεσις. –Καὶ
pass_a_gloss: letter, as much power as we have, we ought to help the poor who are oppressed by the powerful. Verse 15: And a foot to a lame one. He also granted even to those lamed in the bases the feet of the soul; and by the word he himself became their foot. Verse 16: And a judgment which I did not know, I tracked out. He teaches us how one must judge, if ever we are called upon a settlement of brothers, so as to settle the things according to them. Chapter 32 verse 1: And Job ceased with words. And his three friends also were quiet still to speak against Job. For Job was righteous opposite them. He did not simply cease. But his heart understanding the divine things did not cease. For already there is a time for every matter under heaven, a time of being silent and a time of speaking. When then it was time to answer toward the three, he spoke; when it was time, after silencing them, he was silent. And I think it is said in praise: Job ceased. Verse 7: Therefore I was quiet, fearing to announce to you my own knowledge. He has knowledge how humans suffer; why humans come into certain circumstances in this life alone; how many being unjust prosper. I saw those doing injustice and lawless things, and my feet were almost shaken. If I look only in this life, my steps were nearly poured out. Verse 10: Not the long timed ones are wise. For it is not necessary, he says, that only the elders be wise; but it is possible also from youth to hear something noble. For if time makes wise ones, much more God. Verse 18: For the spirit of the belly destroys me. Just as someone becomes pregnant, and the one being born having been formed in him, he comes upon birth pains, until he bears this which he formerly conceived; think something such also to have happened upon the soul of the love of learning. For it conceives the word which, being announced, it forms and stamps with order. And whenever after stamping and forming it, having become ready, it does not hand over as an unready and incomplete miscarriage, but as brought to term and perfected I would say. Verse 19: And my belly is like a wineskin of new wine boiling, bound. It seems to me that from here has been said that in the Gospel. 17.96 No one puts new wine into old wineskins. Verse 20: I will speak, so that I may rest having opened the lips. The one attaining a understanding hearer, and being full of words, speaking rests, and says: I will speak, so that I may rest. Verse 22: For I do not know how to wonder at a face. For I do not know how to wonder at a face. I do not have this knowledge, so that I may wonder at a face; but I despise humans, and the shame from them of mortals, and the embarrassment from them. Verse 22: And if not, moths will also eat me. As of the moths eating through those who take faces of humans. Chapter 35 verse: If you have sinned, what will you do? If you look up into heaven and observe the clouds, you will understand what you have sinned. What must you do? Approach the high priest, and entreat, so that the high priest may bring a sacrifice about you. For if someone sins, we have an advocate toward the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous, and he himself is a propitiation about our sins. Verse: And if you have also done many lawless deeds, what can you do? You will do the so great thing; you will dissolve your many lawless deeds. For this reason upon the incurable things which we cannot heal ourselves, Jesus Christ came from heavens, so that he may heal the incurable, and there may come to be: Blessed are those whose lawless deeds have been forgiven, and whose sins have been covered. Verse 7: Since then you are righteous, what will you give him? But if you are righteous as toward God, what do you have to give according to your righteousness? And if also as you say you are righteous, what will you add to him? Verse 10: The one arranging night watches. Praises of God, and praises and hymns of him he goes through. The one arranging night watches — he himself is God. I want to see how God is arranging night watches. Wholly this age is night; it is darkness. The light is kept for you. What you see now as light, you see through a mirror; And in your light we will see light. We are going sometime to see it. Therefore all the age is night; since it is night, many wars, many wild beasts go about. Verse 11: The one marking me off from four footed ones of earth. If you are a sinner, you have not been marked off from the four footed ones of earth. For a human being in honor did not understand. He was compared to the senseless cattle, and was likened to them. If you are a sinner, you have not been marked off from the four footed ones of the earth; but it is said to you: Do not become as horse and mule, in which there is not 17.97 understanding. — And
pass_b_english: letter: as far as our power goes, we ought to help the poor oppressed by the powerful. "[[And a foot to a lame one >> Bible:Job 29:15]]:" he granted feet of the soul even to those lamed in their bases, and by the word he himself became their foot. "[[A judgment which I did not know, I tracked out >> Bible:Job 29:16]]:" he teaches how to judge when called to settle brothers affairs.

Chapter 32: "[[And Job ceased with words >> Bible:Job 32:1]]." The three friends were quiet still to speak against him, for he was righteous opposite them. He did not simply cease; the heart understanding divine things did not cease. "[[There is a time for every matter under heaven, a time to be silent and a time to speak >> Bible:Ecclesiastes 3:1]]." When it was time to answer the three, he spoke; after silencing them, he was silent — said in praise: Job ceased. Elihu: "[[I was quiet, fearing to announce my own knowledge >> Bible:Job 32:6]]." He knows how humans suffer, why they fall into circumstances in this life alone, how the unjust prosper. I saw those doing injustice, and my feet were almost shaken. If I look only in this life, my steps were nearly poured out. "[[Not the long-timed ones are wise >> Bible:Job 32:9]]:" not only elders; youth can hear something noble. If time makes wise, much more God.

"[[The spirit of the belly destroys me >> Bible:Job 32:18]]." As a pregnant person comes to birth-pains until the formed child is born, so the love-of-learning soul conceives a word, forms and stamps it in order, and when ready does not hand over a miscarriage but something brought to term. "[[My belly is like a wineskin of new wine boiling, bound >> Bible:Job 32:19]]" — from here, Origen thinks, the Gospel: "[[No one puts new wine into old wineskins >> Bible:Matthew 9:17]]." "[[I will speak so that I may rest having opened the lips >> Bible:Job 32:20]]:" full of words before an understanding hearer, speaking rests. "[[I do not know how to wonder at a face >> Bible:Job 32:21]]; if not, moths will eat me" — moths eat those who take human faces.

Chapter 35: "[[If you have sinned, what will you do? >> Bible:Job 35:6]]" Look up to heaven and clouds and understand the sin. Approach the high priest so he may bring sacrifice: "[[If anyone sins, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous, and he is the propitiation for our sins >> Bible:1 John 2:1-2]]." If many lawless deeds, what can you do? Dissolve them — for the incurable we cannot heal, Christ came from heaven: "[[Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are forgiven and whose sins are covered >> Bible:Psalm 32:1]]." "[[Since you are righteous, what will you give him? >> Bible:Job 35:7]]" What can righteousness add to God? "[[The one arranging night watches >> Bible:Job 35:10]]" is God. This whole age is night and darkness; light is kept for you. What you see now you see through a mirror; "[[in your light we will see light >> Bible:Psalm 36:9]]." Because it is night, many wars and wild beasts go about. "[[The one marking me off from four-footed ones of earth >> Bible:Job 35:11]]." If you are a sinner you are not marked off: "[[a human in honor did not understand; he was compared to senseless cattle >> Bible:Psalm 49:12]]; "[[do not become as horse and mule, which have no understanding >> Bible:Psalm 32:9]]." — And
